The paper presents a new method for solving boundary-value problems in potential theory and electromagnetic scattering.
The method uses a conserved-flux concept and a single expansion for tangential electric and magnetic fields.
The method is applied to electrostatic, magnetostatic, and electromagnetic cases.
The results are compared with existing work and new analytical results are obtained from the infinite matrix equations.
The method reduces the number of equations and unknowns needed for a given accuracy.
The dynamical equations reduce to the static case in the low-frequency limit.
The power radiated out through the surface is equal to the power transmitted into the medium, less the power absorbed in the intervening volume.
The conserved-flux concept allows for the derivation of T-matrix equations without recourse to the Huygens principle or physically fictitious fields.
The method uses a single expansion for tangential electric and magnetic fields, which cuts the computation in half.
The matrix elements RI and R2 are used to determine the surface field coefficients a and the induced-field coefficients /.
The orthonormality relations associated with the vector spherical harmonics are used to compute the scattered field.
The power absorbed in the intervening volume is proportional to the conductivity of the medium.
The method is applicable to both lossless and dissipative media.
The results are compared with existing work and new analytical results are obtained from the infinite matrix equations.
